## Context / Problem
`reconciler/alert_store.patch_bug_filed` (`src/rebar/reconciler/alert_store.py:100-147`) reads a day's `*.jsonl` alert file, patches one record and republishes the whole file through `_atomic_write`, without holding the append lock. `append` writes the same file under `sibling_exclusive_lock(today, lock_name=_APPEND_LOCK_NAME)` (`:49`). An alert appended between the patch's `read_text` (`:123`) and its replace (`:144`) is dropped by the replace, on every platform. Found while enumerating readers for ruby-unwomanish-willet; this is a lost-update race, not that bug's Windows read refusal.

## Approach
Hold the same `sibling_exclusive_lock(jf, lock_name=_APPEND_LOCK_NAME)` across the read-modify-write of each file in `patch_bug_filed`, so a patch and an append are serialized.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/reconciler/alert_store.py`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_alert_store_patch_lock.py` (new)

## Testing
A unit test starts `patch_bug_filed` with its read paused (monkeypatched `_atomic_write` that waits on an event), appends an alert from another thread, then releases the patch; the appended record must survive. It fails on the current code and passes with the lock held.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The new test fails on origin/main before the change and passes after it.
- [x] `make verify` passes.
